Entry: Beginning of Spring — daily living rhythm
KeyPoints: Yang qi begins to arise at the start of spring. Sleep later and rise earlier, stretch the limbs and tendons, and keep the diet light on sour and generous on sweet.
Source: Huangdi Neijing · Suwen · Ch. 2 — On Nurturing Spirit in the Four Seasons, Spring section: "In the three months of spring, all things begin to germinate. Heaven and earth are born together, and all things flourish; sleep late and rise early, walk widely in the courtyard, let the hair down and loosen the form, so that the intention may arise… this is the response to spring qi, the way of nurturing life."
Programs: Warm moxibustion service; Wellness consultation service
Notes: English edition. Fully translated from the Chinese SSOT entry.

KeyPoints: Day and night are of equal length at the spring equinox. Keep the routine regular, the mood even, and the diet balanced.
Source: Huangdi Neijing · Suwen · Ch. 2 — On Nurturing Spirit in the Four Seasons: "Yin and yang of the four seasons are the root of all things. Therefore the sages nourish yang in spring and summer, and nourish yin in autumn and winter, in order to follow their root, and thus move and sink with all things in the gate of growth and decline."
Notes: English edition. Fully translated from the Chinese SSOT entry.

KeyPoints: Yang qi is at its height at the summer solstice. Sleep late and rise early, stay out of the heat, and keep the food light.
Source: Huangdi Neijing · Suwen · Ch. 2 — On Nurturing Spirit in the Four Seasons, Summer section: "In the three months of summer, all things flourish. Heaven and earth exchange qi, and all things bear fruit; sleep late and rise early, do not grow weary of the sun, let the intention not be angry, let the flowers and leaves mature, and let the qi flow out… this is the response to summer qi, the way of nourishing and growing."
Programs: Warm moxibustion service; Wellness consultation service
Notes: English edition. Fully translated from the Chinese SSOT entry.

KeyPoints: At major heat the summer heat is at its peak. Rest away from the heat, keep the food light and low in fat, and do not chase coolness.
Source: Huangdi Neijing · Suwen · Ch. 2 — On Nurturing Spirit in the Four Seasons, Summer section: "Let the qi flow out… this is the response to summer qi, the way of nourishing and growing." Same chapter: "Because of summer heat, the sweat, vexation and panting… the body as if it were burning charcoal, the sweat flows out and it disperses."
Notes: English edition. Fully translated from the Chinese SSOT entry.

Entry: Beginning of Autumn — daily living rhythm
KeyPoints: The summer heat has not yet gone at the beginning of autumn. Sleep early and rise early, guard against autumn dryness, and keep the diet moistening.
Source: Huangdi Neijing · Suwen · Ch. 2 — On Nurturing Spirit in the Four Seasons, Autumn section: "In the three months of autumn, all things are brought to maturity. The weather is brisk and the earth's qi is clear; sleep early and rise early, rising and resting with the rooster, let the intention be at peace to soften the punishment of autumn, gather in the spirit so that autumn qi is level, do not let the intention go out, let the lung qi be clear; this is the response to autumn qi, the way of nourishing and gathering."
Programs: Warm moxibustion service; Wellness consultation service
Notes: English edition. Fully translated from the Chinese SSOT entry.

KeyPoints: The gap between day and night temperature widens at white dew. Add a layer for warmth, and keep the diet warm and moistening.
Source: Huangdi Neijing · Suwen · Ch. 3 — On the Connection Between Man and Nature: "Therefore in the evening one gathers and closes, does not disturb the sinews and bones, does not go out into fog and dew; contrary to these three seasons, the body becomes thin and wearied." Same chapter: "Yang qi rules the exterior during the day; in the early morning human qi begins, at noon yang qi is at its peak, in the west yang qi is already weak, and the qi gate closes."
Notes: English edition. Fully translated from the Chinese SSOT entry.

KeyPoints: At the autumn equinox, sleep early and rise early, guard against chill and dryness, and keep the mood even.
Source: Huangdi Neijing · Suwen · Ch. 2 — On Nurturing Spirit in the Four Seasons, Autumn section: "Let the intention be at peace to soften the punishment of autumn, gather in the spirit so that autumn qi is level, do not let the intention go out, let the lung qi be clear."
Notes: English edition. Fully translated from the Chinese SSOT entry.

KeyPoints: At frost's descent, keep warm, guard against the cold, avoid raw and cold food, and tonify moderately.
Source: Huangdi Neijing · Suwen · Ch. 2 — On Nurturing Spirit in the Four Seasons, Winter section: "In the three months of winter, all things are stored away. The water freezes and the earth cracks; do not disturb yang, sleep early and rise late, waiting for the sunlight, let the intention be as if hidden and as if something private were achieved, go away from the cold and toward warmth, do not let it leak out of the skin… this is the response to winter qi, the way of nourishing and storing."
Programs: Warm moxibustion service; Wellness consultation service
Notes: English edition. Fully translated from the Chinese SSOT entry.

Entry: Beginning of Winter — daily living rhythm
KeyPoints: Yang qi begins to close at the beginning of winter. Sleep early and rise late, warm and preserve yang, and keep the diet warm.
Source: Huangdi Neijing · Suwen · Ch. 2 — On Nurturing Spirit in the Four Seasons, Winter section: "Sleep early and rise late, waiting for the sunlight… this is the response to winter qi, the way of nourishing and storing."
Programs: Warm moxibustion service; Wellness consultation service
Notes: English edition. Fully translated from the Chinese SSOT entry.

KeyPoints: At the winter solstice yin reaches its extreme and yang is born. Rest quietly and store the spirit, and keep the diet warm and tonifying.
Source: Huangdi Neijing · Suwen · Ch. 2 — On Nurturing Spirit in the Four Seasons: "Yin and yang of the four seasons are the root of all things. Therefore the sages nourish yang in spring and summer, and nourish yin in autumn and winter, in order to follow their root." Same chapter, Winter section: "Sleep early and rise late, waiting for the sunlight… this is the response to winter qi, the way of nourishing and storing."
Programs: Warm moxibustion service; Wellness consultation service
Notes: English edition. Fully translated from the Chinese SSOT entry.

Entry: Minor Cold and Major Cold — daily living rhythm
KeyPoints: Through minor cold and major cold, keep stored and guard against cold, sleep early and rise late, and do not stay up late and drain yang.
Source: Huangdi Neijing · Suwen · Ch. 2 — On Nurturing Spirit in the Four Seasons, Winter section: "The water freezes and the earth cracks; do not disturb yang, sleep early and rise late, waiting for the sunlight… go away from the cold and toward warmth, do not let it leak out of the skin, and let the qi be drawn in. This is the response to winter qi, the way of nourishing and storing."
Notes: English edition. Fully translated from the Chinese SSOT entry.

Entry: Rain Water and Awakening of Insects — daily living rhythm
KeyPoints: Damp rises around rain water and the awakening of insects. Keep the diet light and low in richness, and keep the room ventilated.
Source: Huangdi Neijing · Suwen · Ch. 2 — On Nurturing Spirit in the Four Seasons, Spring section: "Heaven and earth are born together, and all things flourish; sleep late and rise early, walk widely in the courtyard, let the hair down and loosen the form, so that the intention may arise." Same chapter, Winter section: "Go away from the cold and toward warmth, do not let it leak out of the skin."
Programs: Bian-stone warm compress service; Wellness consultation service
Notes: English edition. Fully translated from the Chinese SSOT entry.

Entry: Pure Brightness and Grain Rain — daily living rhythm
KeyPoints: Damp is heavy during pure brightness and grain rain. Keep the diet warm rather than rich, and keep the room ventilated and dry.
Source: Huangdi Neijing · Suwen · Ch. 3 — On the Connection Between Man and Nature: "Therefore spring injures one with wind, the pathogenic qi lingers and stays, and this becomes diarrhoea." Same chapter: "Because of damp, the head is as if wrapped; damp-heat is not dispelled, the large sinews shorten and become tight, the small sinews relax and lengthen."
Notes: English edition. Fully translated from the Chinese SSOT entry.

Entry: Grain in Ear and Minor Heat — daily living rhythm
KeyPoints: Damp and heat both press during grain in ear and minor heat. Keep the diet light, and avoid heavy, congesting flavours.
Source: Huangdi Neijing · Suwen · Ch. 3 — On the Connection Between Man and Nature: "Because of summer heat, the sweat, vexation and panting; at rest there is much talk, the body is as if it were burning charcoal, the sweat flows out and it disperses." Same chapter: "Because of damp, the head is as if wrapped; damp-heat is not dispelled."
Notes: English edition. Fully translated from the Chinese SSOT entry.

Entry: End of Heat — daily living rhythm
KeyPoints: The summer heat begins to retreat at end of heat. Sleep early and rise early, guard against chill, and protect the stomach.
Source: Huangdi Neijing · Suwen · Ch. 2 — On Nurturing Spirit in the Four Seasons, Autumn section: "Sleep early and rise early, rising and resting with the rooster, let the intention be at peace to soften the punishment of autumn, gather in the spirit."
Notes: English edition. Fully translated from the Chinese SSOT entry.

Entry: Minor Snow and Major Snow — daily living rhythm
KeyPoints: Through minor snow and major snow the cold is severe. Keep warm, keep the diet warm, and keep the room warm.
Source: Huangdi Neijing · Suwen · Ch. 2 — On Nurturing Spirit in the Four Seasons, Winter section: "The water freezes and the earth cracks; do not disturb yang, sleep early and rise late, waiting for the sunlight… go away from the cold and toward warmth, do not let it leak out of the skin."
Programs: Warm moxibustion service; Wellness consultation service
Notes: English edition. Fully translated from the Chinese SSOT entry.

Entry: The general principle of the four seasons
KeyPoints: The Huangdi Neijing, Suwen, says: nourish yang in spring and summer, nourish yin in autumn and winter.
Source: Huangdi Neijing · Suwen · Ch. 2 — On Nurturing Spirit in the Four Seasons: "Yin and yang of the four seasons are the root of all things. Therefore the sages nourish yang in spring and summer, and nourish yin in autumn and winter, in order to follow their root, and thus move and sink with all things in the gate of growth and decline."
Notes: English edition. Fully translated from the Chinese SSOT entry.

Entry: The general principle of treating before illness
KeyPoints: The Huangdi Neijing, Suwen, says: the sage does not treat illness once it has arisen, nor disorder once it has formed — that is what is meant by it.
Source: Huangdi Neijing · Suwen · Ch. 2 — On Nurturing Spirit in the Four Seasons: "Therefore the sage does not treat illness once it has arisen, but treats what is not yet ill; does not treat disorder once it has formed, but treats what is not yet disordered. This is what is meant by it."
Notes: English edition. Fully translated from the Chinese SSOT entry.

KeyPoints: The Huangdi Neijing, Suwen, says: grains, meats, fruits and vegetables — food-based care uses them fully.
Source: Huangdi Neijing · Suwen · Ch. 14 — On Storing Qi According to the Seasons: "Sour governs contraction, sweet governs supplementation, pungent governs dissemination, bitter governs firmness and drainage, salty governs surging and draining."
Notes: English edition. Fully translated from the Chinese SSOT entry.

Entry: The warning about a regular daily routine
KeyPoints: The Huangdi Neijing, Suwen, says: model yourself on yin and yang, harmonise with the numbers, keep food and drink in moderation, keep the routine regular, and do not labour beyond your capacity — then body and spirit stay together.
Source: Huangdi Neijing · Suwen · Ch. 1 — On the Pristine Simplicity of the Ancients: "Therefore model yourself on yin and yang, harmonise with the numbers, keep food and drink in moderation, keep the routine regular, and do not labour beyond your capacity; thus the body and the spirit stay together, and one lives out the natural span of years."
Notes: English edition. Fully translated from the Chinese SSOT entry.

Entry: The relationship between the emotions and wellbeing
KeyPoints: The Huangdi Neijing, Suwen, says: be calm and free of craving, and the true qi follows; the spirit is kept within, and where does illness come from?
Source: Huangdi Neijing · Suwen · Ch. 1 — On the Pristine Simplicity of the Ancients: "Be calm and free of craving, and the true qi follows; the spirit is kept within, and where does illness come from?"
Notes: English edition. Fully translated from the Chinese SSOT entry.

KeyPoints: The Huangdi Neijing, Suwen, says: with daoyin and anqo, the qi moves and the blood vessels are harmonised.
Source: Huangdi Neijing · Lingshu · Ch. 9 — The Channels: "The channels move the blood and qi, and bring yin and yang together at the cun-kou." See also Huangdi Neijing · Lingshu · Ch. 1 — Nine Needles, Twelve Source Points: "As for the timing of supplementation and draining, the needles are used for it."
Programs: Full-body massage service; Wellness consultation service
Notes: English edition. Fully translated from the Chinese SSOT entry.

Entry: The principle of the four seasons
KeyPoints: The Huangdi Neijing, Suwen, says: this is the response to spring qi, the way of nurturing life.
Source: Huangdi Neijing · Suwen · Ch. 2 — On Nurturing Spirit in the Four Seasons, Spring section: "This is the response to spring qi, the way of nurturing life."
Notes: English edition. Fully translated from the Chinese SSOT entry.

Entry: Yin and yang as the root of all things
KeyPoints: The Huangdi Neijing, Suwen, says: yin and yang of the four seasons are the root of all things.
Source: Huangdi Neijing · Suwen · Ch. 2 — On Nurturing Spirit in the Four Seasons: "Yin and yang of the four seasons are the root of all things."
Notes: English edition. Fully translated from the Chinese SSOT entry.

Entry: The rising and falling of yang through the day
KeyPoints: The Huangdi Neijing, Suwen, says: yang qi rules the exterior during the day; in the early morning human qi begins, at noon yang qi is at its peak, in the west yang qi is already weak, and the qi gate closes.
Source: Huangdi Neijing · Suwen · Ch. 3 — On the Connection Between Man and Nature: "Yang qi rules the exterior during the day; in the early morning human qi begins, at noon yang qi is at its peak, in the west yang qi is already weak, and the qi gate closes."
Notes: English edition. Fully translated from the Chinese SSOT entry.

Entry: The effect of damp on the body
KeyPoints: The Huangdi Neijing, Suwen, says: because of damp, the head is as if wrapped; damp-heat is not dispelled, the large sinews shorten and become tight, the small sinews relax and lengthen.
Source: Huangdi Neijing · Suwen · Ch. 3 — On the Connection Between Man and Nature: "Because of damp, the head is as if wrapped; damp-heat is not dispelled, the large sinews shorten and become tight, the small sinews relax and lengthen."
Programs: Warm moxibustion service; Wellness consultation service
Notes: English edition. Fully translated from the Chinese SSOT entry.

KeyPoints: Warm moxibustion is a non-medical heat therapy service. It suits people with a yang-deficient tendency or cold hands and feet. After a session, stay out of the draught and rest for half an hour.

KeyPoints: Cupping suits people who feel heavy with damp, or who have tightness across the shoulders and upper back.

Entry: Beginning of Summer — daily living rhythm
KeyPoints: Yang qi grows steadily at the beginning of summer. Sleep late and rise early, loosen the limbs, and keep the food light and low in richness.
Source: Huangdi Neijing · Suwen · Ch. 2 — On Nurturing Spirit in the Four Seasons, Summer section: "In the three months of summer, all things flourish. Heaven and earth exchange qi, and all things bear fruit; sleep late and rise early, do not grow weary of the sun, let the intention not be angry, let the flowers and leaves mature, and let the qi flow out… this is the response to summer qi, the way of nourishing and growing."
Notes: English edition. Fully translated from the Chinese SSOT entry.

KeyPoints: Damp and heat build at grain buds. Keep the routine regular, keep the room ventilated, and keep the diet light and low in heavy flavours.
Source: Huangdi Neijing · Suwen · Ch. 3 — On the Connection Between Man and Nature: "Because of damp, the head is as if wrapped; damp-heat is not dispelled, the large sinews shorten and become tight, the small sinews relax and lengthen." Same chapter: "Because of summer heat, the sweat, vexation and panting; at rest there is much talk, the body is as if it were burning charcoal, the sweat flows out and it disperses."
Notes: English edition. Fully translated from the Chinese SSOT entry.

KeyPoints: The dew turns cold at cold dew. Sleep early and rise early, add clothing for warmth, and keep the diet warm, moistening and even.
Source: Huangdi Neijing · Suwen · Ch. 3 — On the Connection Between Man and Nature: "Therefore in the evening one gathers and closes, does not disturb the sinews and bones, does not go out into fog and dew; contrary to these three seasons, the body becomes thin and wearied." Same chapter: "Yang qi rules the exterior during the day; in the early morning human qi begins, at noon yang qi is at its peak, in the west yang qi is already weak, and the qi gate closes."
Programs: Warm moxibustion service; Wellness consultation service
Notes: English edition. Fully translated from the Chinese SSOT entry.
